text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT: CRITICAL - node-gpu-07 (us-west-2a) - host unreachable / kubelet NotReady / possible kernel oops. PD key: PD-9921. Paging eng-oncall rota.

pagerduty: page fired to tyler (eng-oncall) and on-call rota.

tyler (eng-oncall): acked. I'm on it. Pulling up node info.

sophia (eng-sre): FYI I'm watching metrics -> batch inference error spike (~18% 5m error rate on model: rw/gpt-topk) and scheduler backlog on gpu-serving namespace.

tyler (eng-oncall): `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep node-gpu-07` -> `node-gpu-07   NotReady   <none>   4d   v1.27   10.2.5.17   us-west-2a`

tyler (eng-oncall): `kubectl describe node node-gpu-07` shows `KubeletStopped`, `taints: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute`, and a flurry of `kernel: audit: type=1701` messages in node events.

sophia (eng-sre): Can someone SSH into the host and grab `dmesg` / `journalctl -k`? looks like a kernel oops in NVMe driver in recent incidents.

jin (infra): ssh'ed to 10.2.5.17, root access ok but host intermittently unresponsive. pulled last 120 lines of kernel log:

```
[  143.874321] nvme 0000:3b:00.0: aborting command 0x5 status: 0x80
[  143.874329] nvme 0000:3b:00.0: failed to read queue 0 doorbell
[  143.876110] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000008
[  143.876118] CPU: 1 PID: 1174 Comm: kubelet Not tainted 5.19.0-rc1 #1
[  143.876120] Call Trace:
[  143.876121]  <stack trace elided>
[  143.876122] kernel panic - not syncing: fatal exception
```

tyler (eng-oncall): kernel panic confirmed. Likely hardware/driver crash leading to kubelet unready. This is a full host-level fault, not just kubelet.

sophia (eng-sre): Immediate mitigation: cordon + drain to move pods off. But drain may hang if node kernel panicked. We'll need to force delete pods that are stuck and scale up replacement capacity.

tyler (eng-oncall): executing safe steps now: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-07` -> done.

tyler (eng-oncall): Attempting drain: `kubectl drain node-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` -> many pods stuck terminating.

jin (infra): I'm starting a replacement instance from the Dedicated GPU pool (flavor: p4d-like), will attach same taints/labels, and start kubelet join. ETA ~6-8 minutes. Also opening a hardware ticket with cloud provider for nvme errors.

ashley (customer-success): Heads up - AcmeSearch reported elevated 504 errors in their inference route 3m ago. They're pinging CS. Can we estimate affected customers and ETA?

sophia (eng-sre): Quick impact note: ~11% of production GPU capacity in us-west-2a offline; RLQ batch jobs hitting queuing; live-serving fallback configured to route to us-west-2b and dedicated reserves but some requests queued resulting in latency/error spike. We're mitigating by scaling up spare capacity in us-west-2b and temporarily relaxing concurrency limits for critical routes.

tyler (eng-oncall): Force-deleting 6 stuck pods now: `kubectl get pods -n gpu-serving --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-gpu-07` then `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force ...` -> done, most moved to other nodes or waiting in pending while new node joins.

jin (infra): New node `node-gpu-13` provisioning; kubelet joined cluster, labels/taints copied: `gpu=true, pool=dedicated`, ready in 5m. Starting cordon/un-cordon dance to rebalance.

sophia (eng-sre): Routing table change: automatic fallback complete; error rate trending down to baseline (5m error now ~3%). We'll keep traffic steering for 10 minutes then re-evaluate.

ashley (customer-success): Update sent to AcmeSearch: "We've routed your traffic to healthy capacity and are seeing error rates decline. We'll follow up with RCA." They acknowledged.

tyler (eng-oncall): Opening internal incident ticket: INC-2027. Assigning to infra + hardware + runtime. Log summary and actions in ticket.

jin (infra): Cloud provider case opened (Case #CP-8812) for NVMe controller errors and kernel panic. Boot logs captured and attached. Starting host repro attempt in isolated lab rack.

tyler (eng-oncall): I'm handing off active recovery to jin (infra) for hardware remediation and to sophia for SRE follow-up on autoscaling/capacity settings. I'll remain on watch for 15 minutes then step back.

sophia (eng-sre): Noted. We'll keep the monitoring playbook running. Schedule: full postmortem to be submitted in 48 hours with kernel oops traces, hardware logs, and mitigation plan (taint/eviction improvements + automated replacement).

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: PD-9921 acknowledged by tyler at 2071234580, resolved? no - continued followups under INC-2027. Escalation canceled.

tyler (eng-oncall): closing the immediate alert thread here — node recovered via replacement, traffic stabilized. Leaving open for postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Monitoring: No further critical alerts for node-gpu-07 group in the last 10m.
